COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLR No. 125 of 2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Pradeep Kumar Chauhan, learned 
counsel for the revisionist.
2. Mr. Nikhil Singhal, learned counsel 
for the respondent.
3. The instant revision has been 
preferred under Section 25 of the 
Provincial Small Causes Courts Act, 1887 
against the judgment and order dated 
04.11.2025, passed by District and 
Sessions Judge, Haridwar in SCC Suit No. 
41 of 2024, titled as “Manish Gupta vs. 
Ashok Sharma” whereby the application 
moved under Order 7 Rule 11 read with 
Section 151 C.P.C. has been rejected.
4. Mr. Pradeep Kumar Chauhan, learned 
counsel for the revisionist, on instructions, 
apprise to this Court that the revisionist is 
ready to vacate the property in question, 
however, he prays that two years time 
may be given to the revisionist to vacate 
the property in question.
5. On the other side, Mr. Nikhil Singhal, 
learned counsel for the respondent have 
accepted the proposal of Mr. P.K.Chauhan.
6. In view of submissions as made 
above and particularly taking into 
consideration that the revisionist is ready 
to vacate the property in question within 
two years, the instant revision is disposed 
of finally with a direction to the revisionist 
to vacate the property in question on or 
before 31.10.2027.
7. In reference to the aforesaid 
undertaking the revisionist shall file an 
affidavit before the District and Sessions 
Judge Haridwar within two weeks 
positively from today.
8. It is further made clear that if the 
revisionist breach any undertaking given 
above the respondent shall apprise to this  2025:UHC:9993
Court by moving an application so that the 
appropriate steps shall be taken against 
the revisionist.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
12.11.2025
Nahid

CLR No. 125 of 2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. P.K. Chauhan, learned counsel 
for the revisionist through V.C.
2. Mr. Nikhil Singhal, learned counsel 
for the respondent.
3. Clarification application MCC No. 2 
of 2025 has been moved by the 
respondent/landlord by submitting that 
actual rent of the shop in question is Rs. 
50,000/- per month which is evident 
from the account statement which 
pertains to the deposit of rent of two 
months, i.e., May and June 2023. Apart 
from this, Mr. Nikhil Singhal, learned 
counsel submits that the revisionist 
already owned two commercial shops in 
the same locality, the photographs of 
which is enclosed at page 93 and 95 of 
the clarification application since mobile 
no. of the revisionist is shown in the sign 
board. He also placed before this Court 
the photocopy of the sale deed of the 
mother of the revisionist wherein 
revisionist constructed commercial shop.
5. Mr. Pradeep Chauhan, learned 
counsel who appears for the revisionist 
denied all these facts and submits that
commercial building as shown in the
photographs at page no. 93 and 95 does 
not belong to the revisionist.
6. In such view of the matter, 
concerned Tehsildar is directed to go on 
the spot to verify whether the  photographs as shown at page 93 and 95 
belongs to the revisionist Ashok Sharma 
or not and also verify the sale deed 
dated 24.11.2021 and submit its report 
positively by 06.01.2026.
7. Mr. Nikhil Singhal shall provide 
photographs as well as copy of sale deed 
to Mr. Pradeep Hairiya today itself so 
that Mr. Hairiya communicate the 
concerned Tehsildar today itself. 
8. Put up this matter on 07.01.2026.
 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
03.01.2026
Parul

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CLR No. 125 of 2025
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. P.K. Chauhan, learned counsel for the revisionist. 
2. Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel and 
Mr. Tarun Mohan, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. In compliance of the previous order, Tehsildar, 
Haridwar has placed his report dated 06.01.2026 before this 
Court, which is taken on record. 
4. The details of workshop mentioned at paragraph 1 is 
owned by respondent – plaintiff and is under the tenancy of 
revisionist. Property no. 2 mentioned at paragraph 2 is 
owned by mother of the revisionist where she is running a 
workshop in the name of SSD Motors with GST registration 
in the name of brother of revisionist. Third property 
mentioned at paragraph 3 is owned by the brother of 
revisionist. 
5. The Tehsildar also record the statement of revisionist 
wherein he has stated that two workshops are registered, 
out of which, one workshop is running in the property of 
her mother and one workshop, which is not registered, is 
run by the brother of the revisionist in the property of 
respondent. 
6. Revisionist to get instructions by day after tomorrow 
from her mother whether she is ready to shift one of the 
workshops in her property.
7. List on 09.01.2026.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 07.01.2026

3. Though mention was made and Mr. Singhal also

facts before this court.

Sharma, the brother of the revisionist. The photographs 
is also enclosed along with this report.

an employee in Shri S.S.D. Motors.

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 125 of 2025
Ashok Sharma 
--Petitioner
Versus
Manish Gupta 
--Respondent
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Pradeep Kumar Chauhan, learned counsel for the applicant.
Mr. Nikhil Singhal, learned counsel for the caveator.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Order Reserved on: 27.07.2026
 Order Delivered on: 18.08.2026 
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. The instant civil revision was disposed of finally on 
12.11.2025 on an undertaking of the revisionist that he is ready 
to vacate the shop in question provided he may be given two 
years’ time to vacate, which was also accepted by the 
respondent, consequently, revisionist was directed to vacate the 
shop in question on or before 31.10.2027.
2. Thereafter, a clarification/modification application 
bearing MCC No. 01 of 2025 was moved on behalf of the 
revisionist for seeking clarification of the order dated 12.11.2025,
that monthly rent of the shop is Rs. 18,000/-.
3. Thereafter, another application i.e. MCC No. 02 of 2025 is
moved by the respondent for seeking clarification/modification 
of the same order dated 12.11.2025 to the effect that the 
1 UKHC010177972025
2025:UHC:9993
revisionist be restrained to sub-let the shop under his tenancy 
and shall not change it’s nature and revisionist be directed to 
pay use and occupational charges at the admitted rate of Rs. 
50,000/- per month.
In support of such clarification as sought it is contended in 
paragraph 5 that market rent of the property in question is Rs. 
50,000/- per month and as per the Account Statement the 
revisionist also paid rent at the rate of Rs. 50,000/- as per entry 
dated 07.05.2023 and 23.06.2023 along with the copy of an 
agreement as well as rent deed of property situated in the same 
vicinity in order to establish that the market rent in the locality 
is at Rs. 1 lakh per month. In addition to this, further reference is 
also made that the revisionist is also having commercial 
property in the same locality where he is running similar 
business in the name and style of SSD Motors by placing on 
record some photographs.
4. Thereafter, another MCC No. 03 of 2026 is also filed by 
the revisionist by raising an objection to the 
clarification/modification as sought by the respondent by 
annexing the rent agreement dated 23.10.2020 in order to show 
that the clarification as sought with regard monthly rent at the 
rate of Rs. 50,000/- is misconceived.
5. Thereafter, another MCC No. 04 of 2026 is moved by the 
revisionist for recalling a subsequent order dated 26.02.2026, 
whereby, the counsel for the revisionist was directed to get 
instructions within how much period he will vacate the shop in 
question and by moving this application the revisionist make an 
attempt to twist the entire issue and also touch the merit though 
2 UKHC010177972025
2025:UHC:9993
on the first day the revisionist himself undertakes to vacate the 
shop.
On this MCC 04 of 2026 a further objection is filed by the 
respondent by giving reference of the report of Tehsildar which 
in fact was invited by this court by virtue of order dated 
07.01.2026 and submits that the mother of revisionist running 
also a workshop in the same locality in the name of SSD Motors 
and another property is also owned by the brother of the 
revisionist.
6. Subsequently, an additional affidavit was further filed on 
09.06.2026 by the revisionist in compliance to the order passed 
by this court on 09.06.2026, whereby, this court take serious note 
of giving false statement by the revisionist about two other 
properties in the same locality.
7. Subsequent thereto, a supplementary affidavit has been 
filed along with IA No. 06 of 2026 on 16.06.2026 by the 
revisionist, wherein, the revisionist also gives reference of a First 
Information Report dated 15.06.2023 with regard to a different 
issue, however, which has no relevance which itself shows that 
the revisionist is deliberately diverting the issue.
8. Now, what this court has observed that though revision 
was disposed of finally on 12.11.2025 on an undertaking of the 
revisionist, despite this, both the sides are repeatedly filing 
applications by raising disputing question of fact. Apart from 
this, the revisionist has also not come up with clean hands as he 
has not disclosed other commercial properties wherein he is 
already running two workshops in the same locality, one in the 
name of “SSD Motors”, and another one, wherein, his brother is 
shown to be an employee of the workshop.
3 UKHC010177972025
2025:UHC:9993
9. To verify about two other commercial properties, which 
are under the effective control of the revisionist the Tehsildar
also submit a report on 06.01.2026 and after perusing the report 
of Tehsildar the learned counsel for the revisionist was directed 
to get instructions within how much period he will vacate the 
shop in question but shall not seek more than two months, 
which is reflected from the order dated 26.02.2026. This time 
was reduced provisionally because as per the report of 
Tehsildar there are two other workshops in the same locality 
run by the revisionist and as apprised by Mr. Nikhil Singhal 
both the workshops are under the effective control of the 
revisionist since in one of the workshop the brother is being 
shown as an employee and in another one Mobile number of 
revisionist is reflected from the Sign Board.
10. The subsequent order dated 09.06.2026 reflects the report 
of Tehsildar and after gone through the report and one another 
document i.e. paper no. 18C/2 this court observed that the 
revisionist making a false statement by giving impression that 
SSD Motor Workshop is being run by his brother Aadesh 
Sharma, whereas , paper 18C reveals his brother is the employee 
in the said workshop, not only his in the workshop, which is 
being run in the name of M/S SSD Motors, the mobile number 
of the revisionist is also reflected from the sign board. Now, at 
this juncture, the relevant extract of the order dated 09.06.2026 is 
also being extracted herein as under:
1. “The revisionist is present in court pursuant to the 
previous order when a specific question is asked from him 
that how many workshops are being run in the locality where 
he is running separate workshop in a rental accommodation, 
he submits that he is running only one workshop and other 
one is being run by his brother Aadesh Sharma.

sq.ft., which was purchased for residential purposes a motor 
workshop in the name of M/s S.S.D. Motors is being run, 
which is in the name of Aadesh Sharma, the brother of the 
revisionist. The photographs is also enclosed along with this 
report. 
5. Mr. Nikhil Singhal placed before this court one of the 
document i.e. Paper No. 18C/2, wherein, the brother of the 
revisionist Aadesh Sharma is shown as an employee in Shri 
S.S.D. Motors. 
6. It appears that the revisionist is making a false 
statement by giving impression that the S.S.D. Motors 
workshop is being run by his brother Aadesh Sharma, 
whereas Paper No. 8C/2 reveals that his brother is working as 
an employee in this motor workshop. Not only this, written 
statement filed in the Trial Court also reveals that misleading

statement has been given that Plot measuring 1825 sq.ft. was 
purchased only for residential purposes though as per the 
report of Tehsildar it is being used for commercial purposes. 
Giving a false statement amounts to perjury with the court. 
The revisionist, who is present in court, is directed to file his 
response why he may not be prosecuted for giving a false 
statement in court within 48 hours.”
11. Now, filing of the frequent applications by the revisionist 
as well as by the respondent it reveals that after disposal of the 
revision the parties are unnecessarily wasting time of the court 
by filing frequent applications raising disputed question of the 
fact again and again though this court is of the firm opinion that 
the revisionist has also not approached with clean hands and he 
is not fair with the court and he suppressed about two 
alternative commercial premises, wherein, the two workshops 
are being run by him, still want to retain the shop in question
which is under his tenancy.
12. Therefore, in such an eventuality, when both the parties 
are raising the disputed question of fact though the revision was
already disposed of finally, this court has no option except to 
recall the initial order dated 12.11.2025.
13. Accordingly, the initial order dated 12.11.2025 is recalled 
and the matter is released and to be listed before the another 
Bench.
